title: Karnaugh Maps: Grouping Adjacent Ones
topic: Karnaugh map minimization — a 3-variable function laid out on a 2x4 grid in Gray-code order; adjacent ones grouped into power-of-two rectangles collapse to the simplest sum-of-products form, beating algebra at its own game

beats.narration: There's a way to minimize a Boolean function by drawing — not algebra. Karnaugh maps.

elements.content: Minimize a Boolean expression by drawing instead of algebra?

beats.narration: Take a function of three variables — A, B, C — and assume it's one for these six minterms.

elements.content: six 1's, two 0's — what's the simplest expression?

beats.narration: Lay out a Karnaugh map: A B down the side in Gray code, C across the top. Drop in a one wherever the function equals one.

elements.content: Empty 4x2 K-map grid, AB rows in Gray code (00,01,11,10), C columns (0,1)
Cells fill with 0s and 1s one row at a time
rows ordered so neighbours differ in exactly one variable

beats.narration: Now the magic. Two rectangles cover all six ones. The vertical block is A. The horizontal block is B. Together — A or B.

elements.content: Filled K-map (same as previous beat, persists)
Group 1 — amber rounded rectangle around the bottom 4 cells (AB=11 + AB=10)
Group 2 — rose rounded rectangle around the middle 4 cells (AB=01 + AB=11)
each rectangle of size 2ⁿ erases n variables

beats.narration: F equals A or B. Two terms instead of three — and you didn't have to factor anything.

elements.content: drawing beats algebra for any function up to 4 variables
